text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Bosnia's upcoming local elections will be held in the internationally supervised northern town of Brcko the same way as in the rest of Bosnia, chief of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe, Robert Frowick says in a visit to the disputed Bosnian town.
- An elderly Bosnian Serb, beaten by Moslems in central Bosnia two weeks ago has died of his injuries, United Nation police monitors say.
- A mosque in a village near Croat-controlled southern Bosnian town of Tomislavgrad was dynamited and nearby Moslem houses were damaged as well.

- The agreement on special ties between Bosnian Serbs and Yugoslavia should be suspended until the constitutional court, which still needs to be established, approves it, Moslem co- prime minister in Bosnian government, Haris Silajdzic, says.

- Bosnian Serb parliament session on ratification of the special ties agreement with Yugoslavia and Croatian President visit to Croat-held part of Mostar are aimed at destroying Bosnia. It seems that the Dayton agreement has never taken such heavy blows so far, the daily says in a commentary and asks:"Is Dayton definitely dead?"

- A huge number of Bosnian trucks await entry into Bosnia from Croatia due to a decision by a Croat director of Bosnia's Moslem-Croat federation customs to impose a money deposit on import of goods such as fuel, coffee, alcoholic drinks etc.
